Olanga 1.6.7 for Windows

Timers and live scores beside the orb.

Follow the fourth quarter or keep an eye on your next timer while you work. Both use the same corner of your desktop. When you reach for the Windows taskbar, Olanga gives you room.

Get Olanga for Windows
Preview the desktop cards

Olanga’s desktop cards with sample timers and game data.

Follow your team.

Choose any of the 30 NBA teams in User preferences → Live scores. Golden State is selected to start. During games the card checks ESPN about every 15 seconds, shows the quarter and game clock, and flags delayed updates. You can also show upcoming games and final scores. No API key is required.

Keep time at a glance.

In User preferences → Timer card, pin timers beside Olanga. Use the grip to see up to five timers, just the next one, or a tucked handle. Switch to the game in the same spot. When the last timer is dismissed, its card disappears.

Make room on your desktop.

Drag the score card’s grip to tuck it away while the score keeps updating. The orb’s five-second and one-hour hide options cover both the orb and its card. Point at the bottom taskbar and both disappear. Move away and they return without taking focus.

Control Spotify from Home.

Switch into Olanga and your floating controls give way to Home’s score and music cards. See the current track, pause, resume or skip through Spotify’s Windows media session. The cards stay on Home, and Olanga pauses music polling when you leave that tab.

Forget one detail.

Say “Forget where I live” to remove your saved city and keep your other preferences. If several entries match, Olanga asks which one you mean. You can give a new command while a question is pending, and follow-ups about tasks and timers keep track of the item you’re discussing.

Keep control of unfinished work.

Opening the Routines collection preserves your draft. Switching screen-edit examples clears the previous capture and approval. Undo dismisses any pending question and tells you whether the edit was cancelled, expired or could be reversed.

Already using Olanga?

Open Workspace → Apps & updates, check for updates, then download. Choose Install & restart once Olanga verifies the installer.

0:00 Meet Olanga. A little help, right where you work.

0:05 Play Spotify, set the volume to seventy-five percent, and keep going. Everyday controls stay close, with an orb you can call on from your desktop.

0:19 Coming next: follow the Warriors without leaving your work. Live scores stay nearby during a game. Tuck them away, or bring them inside Olanga.

0:31 Conversations carry context forward. Olanga can pick up useful preferences, recall them later, and use those details when they matter. See what it remembers, and forget anything.

0:45 Turn a familiar start into a routine. Choose your apps, tasks, and focus timer once. Then ask Olanga to run it, review it, and watch your session begin.

0:59 Need a second pair of eyes? Show Olanga what you're working on. Choose the allowed area, then review its proposed steps before approving an edit.

1:15 Find the right file. Preview a clearer set of names, apply the changes, and undo them when you need to.

1:26 Capture an idea in Notepad. Keep the next step in your checklist. Catch up with News. Each has its own place, without breaking the conversation.

1:39 Open a saved workspace. Ask about a project, and follow the answer back to the selected files it came from.

1:50 Make it feel like yours. Check for updates when you're ready.

1:56 Olanga. More done. Stay in your flow.

About this recording

On screen: The actual Olanga interface handles a typed Spotify and volume request with simulated playback results. The real corner orb and score card show sample states; the score updates, the card tucks away, and Home shows its score and music cards. Olanga learns, recalls and forgets a supported preference. A reviewed routine starts a real countdown and adds a checklist item. Desktop assistance shows a sample capture, the allowed edit area and proposed steps, stopping before execution approval. A disposable file is renamed and restored through the real preview, apply and checked-undo flow. Notepad, the Home checklist and News show their actual controls. A saved workspace selects a sample project; local search shows source excerpts before a simulated provider answer. The accent changes through Settings, followed by the start of a manual update check.

About this recording: The app views come from Olanga’s production interface in a local 1.6.5 preview build. Sample Spotify, volume, app-launch, score-feed, News, AI and update responses stand in for external services. The microphone and text-to-speech were muted; commands were typed. Screen planning uses an authored document screenshot and simulated AI response. No native document edit, Google Docs integration or live service result is demonstrated. Timing is edited for the tour and does not measure response speed.

The film shows an earlier preview of the scores and Home cards included in the public 1.6.7 download. Memory, routines, timers, checklist, Notepad and appearance use the app’s local handlers. File rename and undo run on a disposable file, and project search runs on authored local files.
